# Confucius quote sources

17 passages attributed to Confucius in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Confucius.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Confucius

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Classical Chinese

Cited here from

The Analects (Lunyu), cited by book and passage.

How to cite it

Book and passage number, as in Analects 2.17. The numbering is stable across editions, which is why it is worth giving in place of a page — but it should always come with the translator's name, because the English differs enormously between them.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Nothing in the Analects was written by Confucius. It is a collection compiled by later disciples, in which the phrase “The Master said” marks reported speech. The most widely circulated English aphorisms descend from James Legge's nineteenth-century translation, which renders the pronoun 之 as “the truth” — so a sentence that sounds like a timeless maxim is often Legge's diction, not the Chinese.

5 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Confucius?

Book and passage number, as in Analects 2.17. The numbering is stable across editions, which is why it is worth giving in place of a page — but it should always come with the translator's name, because the English differs enormously between them. This archive cites Confucius from The Analects (Lunyu), cited by book and passage. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Confucius?

Nothing in the Analects was written by Confucius. It is a collection compiled by later disciples, in which the phrase “The Master said” marks reported speech. The most widely circulated English aphorisms descend from James Legge's nineteenth-century translation, which renders the pronoun 之 as “the truth” — so a sentence that sounds like a timeless maxim is often Legge's diction, not the Chinese.

### What language did Confucius write in?

Classical Chinese. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
